steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for managing state in React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct import syntax.

steps.title: Create the CachingStrategies component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CachingStrategies that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns null.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Create the CachingStrategies component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named CachingStrategies is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The CachingStrategies component is created and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CachingStrategies component. This sets up the main structure for our caching strategies lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a component named CachingStrategies that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component named CachingStrategies that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for cache data
steps.instruction: Inside the CachingStrategies component, use useState to create a state variable named cacheData initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value and destructure the returned array into cacheData and setCacheData.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a list
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable cacheData that will hold cache data to be displayed and manipulated.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with [] and destructured into cacheData and setCacheData inside the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state for cache data. This empty array will hold the cache entries we'll work with.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] and destructuring it into cacheData and setCacheData.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use useState with an empty array [] inside the component to create the cacheData state variable.

steps.title: Initialize state for selected strategy
steps.instruction: Inside your CachingStrategies component, use useState to create a state variable named selectedStrategy initialized to 'LRU'.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 'LRU' and destructure the returned array into selectedStrategy and setSelectedStrategy.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for tracking selection
const [selectedOption, setSelectedOption] = useState('default');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a selectedStrategy state variable initialized to 'LRU' and a setSelectedStrategy function to update it.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that creates selectedStrategy initialized to 'LRU'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track the selected caching strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with 'LRU' as the initial value and naming the variable selectedStrategy.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectedStrategy state wasn't initialized correctly. Review how to use useState with an initial value.

steps.title: Define helper function to simulate cache operations
steps.instruction: Inside your CachingStrategies component, define a function named simulateCacheOperation that takes a strategy parameter. For now, just create the function with an empty body.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Place it before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a simulateCacheOperation function defined inside your component, ready to implement cache logic in later steps.
successCriteria: The simulateCacheOperation function is defined with a strategy parameter and placed inside the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the simulateCacheOperation function. This will be the core function that handles different caching strategies.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function named simulateCacheOperation that takes a strategy parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Please define a function named simulateCacheOperation that accepts a strategy parameter.

steps.title: Define handler for strategy selection
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleStrategySelect that takes a strategy parameter and updates the selectedStrategy state with it.
steps.hint: Inside your component, create a function that calls setSelectedStrategy with the new strategy value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleStrategySelect function is defined that updates the selectedStrategy state when called.
successCriteria: The handleStrategySelect function is defined, takes a strategy parameter, and calls setSelectedStrategy with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a handler that will update the selected caching strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a parameter and calls setSelectedStrategy with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't update the state correctly. Try creating a function named handleStrategySelect that calls setSelectedStrategy.

steps.title: Return the main container structure
steps.instruction: In your CachingStrategies component, return a div element with the className 'caching-strategies' as the main container.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that has the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with className 'caching-strategies', establishing the main structure for the caching strategies interface.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className 'caching-strategies'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the main container for the caching strategies interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div with exactly className 'caching-strategies'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main container structure isn't correct. Return a div with className 'caching-strategies'.

steps.title: Add header section with title
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add an h1 element with the text 'Caching Strategies'.
steps.hint: Add the h1 element directly inside the container you returned in the previous step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a header element

System Design Patterns
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now displays a header with the lesson title.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Caching Strategies' is present inside the main container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the header section with the lesson title.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a header, but make sure it's an h1 element with the exact text 'Caching Strategies'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header section is missing or incorrect. Add an h1 element with 'Caching Strategies' inside the container.

steps.title: Add strategy selection buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a div element containing three buttons with labels 'LRU', 'LFU', and 'FIFO', and wire each button's onClick event to call handleStrategySelect with the corresponding strategy name.
steps.hint: Create a div with three button elements inside. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls handleStrategySelect with the appropriate string argument.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: Interactive buttons with click handlers
steps.expectedOutcome: A div with three interactive buttons appears in the UI, each representing a caching strategy (LRU, LFU, FIFO). Clicking any button will trigger the handleStrategySelect function.
successCriteria: The component contains a div with three button elements labeled 'LRU', 'LFU', and 'FIFO', each with an onClick handler calling handleStrategySelect with the correct strategy name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added interactive strategy selection buttons. Each button is properly wired to call the selection handler with the corresponding caching strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check that all three strategies (LRU, LFU, FIFO) are represented and each onClick handler correctly calls handleStrategySelect with the appropriate argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The strategy selection buttons are missing or incomplete. Make sure to add a div containing three buttons with labels 'LRU', 'LFU', and 'FIFO', each with onClick handlers that call handleStrategySelect.

steps.title: Display selected strategy information
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the main container that displays the currently selected caching strategy from state.
steps.hint: Use the selectedStrategy state variable inside JSX curly braces to display its value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Display a state value in a paragraph

Current mode: {mode}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing 'Selected strategy: LRU' (or the current selected strategy) appears in the UI.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists that displays the selectedStrategy state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The paragraph now displays the currently selected caching strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the selectedStrategy state value using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the selectedStrategy value correctly.

steps.title: Add simulate operation button
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Simulate Cache Operation' that, when clicked, calls the simulateCacheOperation function with the selectedStrategy as its argument.
steps.hint: Use the onClick event handler on the button to call your simulation function with the current strategy.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: A button that triggers an action
<button onClick={() => handleAction('parameter')}>Perform Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Simulate Cache Operation' appears in the UI, which will trigger the cache simulation when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element is present with the correct text and an onClick handler that calls simulateCacheOperation(selectedStrategy).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the button to trigger cache simulation with the selected strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check the text or onClick handler. It should call simulateCacheOperation with selectedStrategy.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly configured. Add a button with text 'Simulate Cache Operation' and an onClick handler that calls simulateCacheOperation(selectedStrategy).

steps.title: Display cache data visualization
steps.instruction: Add a div element that maps through the cacheData state to display each cache entry as a visual box with key-value pairs.
steps.hint: Use Object.entries(cacheData) to iterate through the cacheData object and render each entry inside a styled div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A visual representation of cache entries appears below the strategy info, showing each key-value pair in a separate box.
successCriteria: The code includes a div that maps through cacheData using Object.entries and displays each entry with key and value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The cache data visualization is now showing each entry clearly, making the cache state visible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some visualization, but make sure to map through all cacheData entries and display both key and value for each.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache data visualization is missing or incorrect. Please add a div that iterates through cacheData to display each entry.
